title_original: Marion Cotillard to Serve as Marrakech Film Festival Jury President

blocks.text: Oscar-winning French actor Marion Cotillard will preside over the competition jury at the 23rd Marrakech Film Festival in November.

Alongside her to be announced jury members, the “Inception” and “Dark Knight Rises” star will lead the decision of which film is awarded the Étoile d’Or out of Marrakech’s international competition, which consists of first and second features.

“I have been fortunate enough to attend the Marrakech International Film Festival since its very beginnings; I’ve had wonderful experiences there and met some truly remarkable people,” Cotillard said in a statement. “Supporting filmmakers as they take their first steps is a vital part of what this festival is all about — it’s in its DNA — and it is a great joy for me to chair the jury this year.”

blocks.text: Cotillard first broke out in the 1998 French action comedy “Taxi,” before making her Hollywood debut in Tim Burton’s “Big Fish” in 2003. In 2007, she portrayed French singer Édith Piaf in “La Vie en Rose” and won the Oscar for best actress, becoming the first actor to win an Academy Award for a French-language performance. She earned her second best actress Oscar nomination in 2015 for the Dardenne Brothers’ drama “Two Days, One Night.”

Most recently, she starred in Guillaume Canet’s Cannes-premiering “Karma,” “Lee” alongside Kate Winslet and on the TV series “The Morning Show” opposite Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon. She is currently filming “The Enraged,” a historical drama from Emmanuelle Bercot.
This year’s Marrakech Film Festival takes place from Nov. 20-28.
